BlueRenderingConfig.description:
Render blues (skies) the way camera JPEGs do: deeper, more colourful, a little cyan.

A camera-matching adjustment in the display transform (ADR-0012), not a creative look.
Measured against the DJI Pocket 4's and DJI drone's JPEGs, an accurate render of a blue
sky is paler, lighter and ~4 degrees more purple than the camera's; the defaults are fitted
to those JPEGs (and checked on held-out photos). Other makers differ (Fujifilm's skies
are close to accurate), so this is the one place the neutral render leans toward DJI's
look. Set ``enabled: false`` for a colorimetric sky.

Applied in display-referred Oklab: a pixel's weight is a raised-cosine window in hue
around ``hue`` (zero beyond ``hue_width``) times a ramp in chroma from ``chroma_start``
to ``chroma_full``, so greys, whites and other hues are untouched.

enabled.description: Apply the camera-matched blue rendering; false leaves blues as the colour matrix and display transform give them (colorimetric).
enabled.title: Enabled

hue.description: Centre of the affected hues (Oklab hue, degrees).
hue.title: Hue

hue_width.description: Hues this far (degrees) or further from the centre are untouched.
hue_width.title: Hue Width

hue_shift.description: Hue rotation at the window's centre (degrees); negative turns blue to cyan.
hue_shift.title: Hue Shift

chroma.description: Chroma (colourfulness) scale at the centre; 1 is none.
chroma.title: Chroma

lightness.description: Lightness scale at the centre; below 1 darkens.
lightness.title: Lightness

chroma_start.description: Oklab chroma below which pixels are untouched (greys and whites).
chroma_start.title: Chroma Start

chroma_full.description: Oklab chroma at and above which the full adjustment applies.
chroma_full.title: Chroma Full

BlueRenderingConfig.title: BlueRenderingConfig

full_lightness.description: Lightness (cube root of luminance, as Oklab L for greys) up to which the full amount applies; 0.2 is 4.5 EV below mid grey.

fade_lightness.description: Lightness at which it has faded out (0.4 is about 1.5 EV below mid grey).

DisplayTransformConfig.description:
The AgX-style display transform (ADR-0003): inset → log encode → sigmoid → outset.

Defaults are our own (ADR-0007), not copied from another implementation: contrast 1.0 and
toe 1.5 keep shadows at least as bright as a plain sRGB view of the linear image (higher
contrast crushed the 2-6 EV below mid grey where most of an unnormalised photo sits);
inset and outset by measuring Oklab hue drift on saturated exposure ramps
(less inset drifts more, more inset desaturates).

min_ev.description: Scene EV (relative to mid grey) that maps to black.
min_ev.title: Min Ev

max_ev.description: Scene EV (relative to mid grey) that maps to white.
max_ev.title: Max Ev

contrast.description: Midtone contrast; 1.0 matches the slope of the plain sRGB curve at mid grey.
contrast.title: Contrast

toe.description: Toe sharpness; higher keeps shadows linear longer.
toe.title: Toe

shoulder.description: Shoulder sharpness; higher keeps highlights linear longer, then rolls off harder.
shoulder.title: Shoulder

inset.description: How far each primary (R, G, B) is pulled toward white before the curve.
inset.title: Inset

chroma_preservation.description: Blend toward a render that keeps each pixel's colour ratios: 0 is pure per-channel AgX (bright colours wash out toward white), 1 keeps highlights fully saturated.
chroma_preservation.title: Chroma Preservation

saturation.description: Overall chroma scale after the curve; 1 is none.
saturation.title: Saturation

saturation_fade.description: How much of the saturation change fades out toward white: 1 = none left at white, 0 = the same everywhere.
saturation_fade.title: Saturation Fade

outset.description: How much saturation each primary (R, G, B) gets back after the curve.
outset.title: Outset

max_correction_ev.description: Largest change correction may make, in EV.

LocalContrastConfig.description:
Keep detail where the display transform's curve flattens it (ADR-0011).

Defaults fitted to camera JPEGs: detail keeps at least ``detail_floor`` display stops per
scene stop, and gets ``amount`` more contrast everywhere.

detail_floor.description: Least contrast detail above mid grey keeps after the display transform, in display stops per scene stop (the curve's shoulder alone gives ~0.2 in a bright sky).
detail_floor.title: Detail Floor

amount.description: Extra detail contrast everywhere; 1 adds none.
amount.title: Amount

radius.description: Size of the broad areas whose brightness the curve sets, as a fraction of the long edge; smaller detail than this counts as detail.
radius.title: Radius

edge_ev.description: Steps in brightness much larger than this (in EV), like a horizon, are kept as edges and not amplified (no halos); smaller ones count as detail.
edge_ev.title: Edge Ev

detail_limit_ev.description: Detail larger than about this many EV (a sun glint, a lamp) is amplified less: what gets added levels off at (gain - 1) times this.
detail_limit_ev.title: Detail Limit Ev

max_gain.description: Most detail is ever amplified, as a factor.
max_gain.title: Max Gain

NormaliseOverrides.description:
One photo's normalise overrides; an unset value keeps the project's or computed one.

``wb_kelvin`` and ``tint`` re-balance the photo from its as-shot white to the white they
describe (scene-linear, before exposure). Either alone keeps the as-shot value of the
other.

enabled.description: Run the normalise stage for this photo; replaces normalise.enabled. false skips it (exposure, white balance and colour noise reduction).
enabled.title: Enabled

wb_kelvin.description: Colour temperature of the light, in kelvin: the photo is re-balanced from its as-shot white to this one. Without tint, keeps the as-shot tint.
wb_kelvin.title: Wb Kelvin

tint.description: Tint of the light, -1000 x Duv: positive is magenta, negative green. Without wb_kelvin, keeps the as-shot colour temperature.
tint.title: Tint

exposure_ev.description: Exposure change for this photo, in EV; replaces the computed one (offset_ev plus any correction).
exposure_ev.title: Exposure Ev

scene_contrast.description: Scene contrast amount for this photo; replaces normalise.scene_contrast.amount and applies even when scene_contrast is off. 0 turns it off for this photo.
scene_contrast.title: Scene Contrast

NormaliseOverrides.title: NormaliseOverrides

OutliersConfig.description:
Ranges a photo's stats should fall in after normalise; outside one, it is an outlier.

An outlier is flagged, never forced back into range. Defaults from the CC0 samples and
the reference set (2026-10-18): medians span -2.5 to +2.3 EV, and only the two dark
scenes the camera brightened more than we do fall below -2.

min_median_ev.description: Darkest median brightness that isn't an outlier, in EV from mid grey.
min_median_ev.title: Min Median Ev

max_median_ev.description: Brightest median brightness that isn't an outlier, in EV from mid grey.
max_median_ev.title: Max Median Ev

max_clipped.description: Largest fraction of pixels clipped by the sensor that isn't an outlier.
max_clipped.title: Max Clipped

OutliersConfig.title: OutliersConfig

long_edge.description: Long edge in pixels; null keeps the full resolution.
long_edge.title: Long Edge

SceneContrastConfig.description:
Extra contrast for flat scenes, as cameras add (ADR-0017).

A scene whose luminance spans less than ``target_range_ev`` between its 5th and 95th
percentiles gets extra contrast ``amount * min(target_range_ev / range - 1, max_contrast)``:
tones are pushed away from the pivot (the ``pivot_percentile`` of the scene's luminance)
by up to ``soft_limit_ev`` times that, the same gain on R, G and B so colours keep their
hue. Off by default: the evidence is two flat photos from one camera.

enabled.description: Add contrast to flat scenes. Off by default until more flat photos confirm it; a photo's scene_contrast override applies even when this is off.
enabled.title: Enabled

amount.description: How much of the extra contrast to apply: 0.5 is gentle (the default), 1.0 matches the camera on the photos it was fitted to, 0 turns it off.
amount.title: Amount

target_range_ev.description: Scenes whose luminance spans less than this between their 5th and 95th percentiles, in EV, get extra contrast; wider scenes are left alone.
target_range_ev.title: Target Range Ev

max_contrast.description: Most extra contrast a very flat scene gets, before amount: 0.5 makes tones near the pivot 50 % steeper.
max_contrast.title: Max Contrast

pivot_percentile.description: Tones at this percentile of the scene's luminance stay put; darker ones get darker, brighter ones brighter. 75 keeps the bright end where it was, as cameras do.
pivot_percentile.title: Pivot Percentile

soft_limit_ev.description: Tones far from the pivot move at most this times the extra contrast, in EV, so deep shadows and highlights are not pushed without limit.
soft_limit_ev.title: Soft Limit Ev

SceneContrastConfig.title: SceneContrastConfig

SharpenConfig.description: Unsharp mask on lightness, at the output's size (after resizing).
SharpenConfig.title: SharpenConfig

WhiteBalanceConfig.description:
The white balance check: compare the as-shot white balance with an estimate.

Normalise keeps the camera's as-shot white balance and always runs the check (its numbers
go into the stats). With ``flag_disagreement`` on, when both estimates from the photo
itself (``brightest`` and ``grey``) differ from it by at least ``flag_disagreement_mired``
in the same direction, the photo gets the ``wb_disagreement`` flag. It is off by default:
genuinely coloured scenes (sunsets, blue sky over foliage) trip it while the as-shot white
balance is right (ADR-0016). Nothing is changed automatically (plan D6). See
:mod:`picturesq.normalise.white_balance_check` for the measurements behind the default.

flag_disagreement.description: Raise wb_disagreement when the estimates disagree with as-shot; off by default because coloured scenes such as sunsets trip it.
flag_disagreement.title: Flag Disagreement

flag_disagreement_mired.description: Flag a photo when both white balance estimates differ from the as-shot one by at least this, the same way, in mired (30 is about 600 K near 4500 K, 1100 K near 6500 K).
flag_disagreement_mired.title: Flag Disagreement Mired

WhiteBalanceConfig.title: WhiteBalanceConfig
